item.mechanism: The addition of Cr promotes the precipitation of the Laves phase (Cr2Ta) due to the strong binding ability between Cr and Ta and the negative enthalpy of mixing, which reduces BCC phase stability.
item.system: WVTaTiCr x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings
item.operating_conditions: Laser cladding process (1.4 kW power, 8 mm/s speed, 6 mm spot diameter), solidification from melt
item.supporting_observation: The minimum enthalpy of mixing (−7 KJ/mol) of Cr and Ta means that during the solidification process, Cr and Ta are more easily combined to form intermetallic compounds, which leads to the formation of Cr 2 Ta in the Laves phase.
item.scope_limits: The authors state that the high-entropy effect effectively inhibits the precipitation of other complex intermetallic compounds beyond the Laves phase.
item.alternatives_considered: The text notes that without Cr, the coating consists mainly of the BCC solid-solution phase without significant Laves precipitation.
quotes: The minimum enthalpy of mixing (−7 KJ/mol) of Cr and Ta means that during the solidification process, Cr and Ta are more easily combined to form intermetallic compounds
the addition of Cr causes more severe lattice distortion in the alloy, thus opening a path for atomic diffusion
the enthalpy of mixing formed between Cr and other refractory elements is small, which reduces the enthalpy value in the alloy and the stability of the BCC phase

item.mechanism: Grain refinement occurs due to rapid solidification from the high-energy laser beam, which creates a large supercooling degree, increases nucleation rate, and limits dendrite growth time.
item.system: WVTaTiCr x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings
item.operating_conditions: Laser cladding with high-energy laser beam, rapid melting and solidification
item.supporting_observation: The laser cladding technology outputs a lot of heat momentarily through a high-energy laser beam, and the pre-set coating melts and solidifies rapidly, which produces a large supercooling degree during solidification
item.scope_limits: This mechanism explains the general hardness increase compared to the substrate but does not explicitly quantify the specific contribution of Cr to grain refinement beyond the general trend.
item.alternatives_considered: The text contrasts this with conventional sintering which leads to embrittlement and porosity, and PVD which has thickness limits.
quotes: produces a large supercooling degree during solidification, increases the nucleation rate, promotes a shorter growth time for each dendrite
collides with other grains, and grows again. The effect of grain refinement is significantly enhanced
with the increase in Cr, the coating grains were more refined

item.mechanism: Hardness increases with Cr content due to a combination of precipitation strengthening from the Laves phase and enhanced solid-solution strengthening.
item.system: WVTaTiCr x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings
item.operating_conditions: Room temperature microhardness testing (1.96 N load, 15 s loading time)
item.supporting_observation: Combining XRD with SEM analysis, with the increase in Cr content, the Laves phase precipitation in the alloy also increases, and the precipitation strengthening effect is enhanced.
item.scope_limits: The text does not provide a specific threshold where hardness might decrease due to excessive brittleness from the Laves phase.
item.alternatives_considered: The text attributes the baseline hardness of the coating to grain refinement, but notes that Cr specifically adds precipitation and solid-solution effects.
quotes: with the increase in Cr content, the average hardness of the coating also increases
the precipitation strengthening effect is enhanced
with the increase in Cr content, the solid-solution strengthening effect in the alloy is enhanced, which further increases the hardness

item.mechanism: High-temperature oxidation resistance improves because Cr addition leads to the formation of a dense, uniform oxide film (containing Cr2O3, TiO2, CrTaO4) that inhibits oxygen diffusion.
item.system: WVTaTiCr x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings
item.supporting_observation: The Cr 1 alloy has the highest oxide diffraction peak, indicating that more oxides are generated, making the oxide film on the coating surface uniform and dense.
item.scope_limits: The mechanism relies on the specific formation of CrTaO4 and Cr2O3; the text notes that Ta2O5 does not appear on the surface due to slow diffusion.
item.alternatives_considered: The text mentions that without Cr (Cr0), the oxide weight gain is significantly higher (10.41 mg/cm2 vs 5.12 mg/cm2 for Cr1).
quotes: The dense oxide film inhibits the diffusion of oxygen atoms, reduces the oxidation rate, and improves oxidation resistance
The addition of Cr makes atomic diffusion slow, and the oxidation rate and weight-gain decrease, thereby improving the high-temperature oxidation resistance of the alloy
the high content of Cr in high-entropy alloys and the slow diffusion effect of high-entropy alloys can improve the high-temperature oxidation resistance

item.mechanism: Corrosion resistance improves in NaCl solution because Cr promotes the generation of a denser, more uniform passive film that reduces ion diffusion and penetration.
item.system: WVTaTiCr x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings
item.operating_conditions: 3.5 wt% NaCl aqueous solution, dynamic polarization electrochemical test
item.supporting_observation: The addition of Cr can promote the generation of the passive film on the surface of the alloy coating, while the oxide deposition of Cr can fill the vacancy of the passive film, making the surface passive film become denser and uniform
item.scope_limits: The text does not specify the pH or temperature range for the corrosion test beyond the stated 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
item.alternatives_considered: The Cr0 alloy showed the lowest corrosion potential (-0.7783 V) and highest corrosion rate (2.959 mm/a), indicating the absence of Cr leads to poor passivation.
quotes: the self-corrosion potential of the alloy gradually increases with the addition of Cr
the WVTaCrTi (Cr 1 ) alloy coating has the highest corrosion potential

item.mechanism: Ta2O5 does not form on the oxidation surface because the atomic radius of Ta is larger than Cr and Ti, leading to a slower diffusion rate that prevents it from reaching the surface to oxidize.
item.system: WVTaTiCr x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings
item.supporting_observation: Due to the atomic radius of Ta being slightly larger than Cr and Ti, the diffusion rate is relatively slow. In addition, there is a lattice distortion effect inside high-entropy alloys, and atomic diffusion needs to overcome varying resistance.
item.scope_limits: This mechanism applies specifically to the 800 °C oxidation environment described; the text does not claim this holds for all temperatures.
item.alternatives_considered: The text notes that TiO2 forms first due to the smallest Gibbs free energy, and Cr2O3 forms despite having a higher Gibbs free energy than Ta2O5 because Cr diffuses faster.
quotes: This slow diffusion effect makes it more difficult for Ta to generate oxides, so Ta 2 O 5 does not appear on the surface
Although the standard Gibbs free energy of molar formation of Cr 2 O 3 is greater than Ta 2 O 5 , the diffusion rate of Cr is faster than Ta
With the addition of Cr, the internal lattice distortion effect of the WVTaTiCr alloy is the strongest, and the diffusion rate of each atom is the slowest

item.mechanism: Laser cladding produces a metallurgical bond with the substrate and a fine microstructure due to the high thermal gradient and rapid cooling rates inherent to the process.
item.operating_conditions: Laser cladding (1.4 kW, 8 mm/s, 30-40% overlap), argon protection
item.supporting_observation: From Figure 1 b,c, it is seen that the metallurgical bonding between the 42CrMo steel and the coating is good, and there are no obvious cracks and pores near the bonding zone (BZ).
item.scope_limits: The text notes that other methods like electrodeposition lead to pores and microcracks, implying this mechanism is specific to the optimized laser cladding parameters used.
item.alternatives_considered: The text contrasts this with magnetron sputtering, PTA welding, and additive manufacturing, noting laser cladding has a smaller heat-affected zone and better bond.
quotes: the cladding layer forms firm metallurgical bonds with the substrate, the heat-affected zone of the coating is small, the deformation of the substrate is small
The results indicate that laser cladding is feasible for the preparation of RHEA coatings
typical dendrite structures are formed near the interface between the coating and the substrate, and grow perpendicular to the boundary

item.mechanism: Elemental segregation occurs during solidification where high-melting-point elements (W, Ta) form dendrites and low-melting-point elements (V, Cr) concentrate in the interdendritic regions.
item.system: WVTaTiCr x (x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1) refractory high-entropy alloy coatings
item.supporting_observation: Ta and W with high melting points are first solidified and formed, and mainly distributed in the white dendrite area; there is a high content of V and Cr elements in the gray area
item.scope_limits: The text notes that Ti is uniformly distributed, distinguishing it from the segregation behavior of other elements.
item.alternatives_considered: The text mentions that the high-entropy effect inhibits the formation of complex intermetallic compounds, suggesting segregation is limited to phase separation rather than compound formation for most elements.
quotes: during the solidification process of the alloy powder, the distribution of elements in the cladding layer is not uniform
Ta and W with high melting points are first solidified and formed, and mainly distributed in the white dendrite area
Ti is uniformly distributed in the alloy
